The incubation period for the single egg is prolonged, with hatching occurring after approximately 23 days [ab = approximately 23 days] when the egg is maintained at a stable incubation temperature of 36 °C [T = 36 °C]. This relatively extended development within the calcareous egg is characteristic of many cotingids and may relate to the substantial yolk reserves required to support the altricial nestling upon emergence.

Neonatal mass represents a critical starting point for the rapid growth phase that follows hatching. Newly hatched chicks weigh approximately 17.9 grams [Ww0 = approximately 17.9 grams], a value that represents the initial wet weight of the individual immediately after emergence from the egg. This size disparity places the species among the larger members of the Cotingidae family, with males exceeding the mass of many sympatric frugivores.
